open_spaces_details.description:
Fellowship Square is a community and creative hub in the heart of Walthamstow. Waltham Forest Town Hall, formerly known as Walthamstow Town Hall, is a Grade II Listed Building in Walthamstow, East London, serving as the headquarters of Waltham Forest London Borough Council. The history of the site dates back to the 19th century, with the original civic building being replaced by an Italianate style town hall in 1866. The current building, designed by Philip Dalton Hepworth in the stripped classical style, was completed in 1942, with interruptions due to World War II. It features a symmetrical main frontage, a tall clock tower, and notable sculptures by John Francis Kavanagh.

In 2019, Hawkins Brown began extensive renovations, aiming to modernise the building while preserving its character. The refurbishment included creating open-plan workspaces and restoring original features like paint samples and Terrazzo flooring. The Town Hall reopened in 2021, accompanied by Fellowship Square, which features a large splash fountain and hosts civic events.
 
Fellowship Square builds on the legacy of Waltham Forest being the first ever Mayor’s London Borough of Culture in 2019. It provides opportunities for new leisure, entertainment and learning spaces, shops and cafes, and provide jobs for local people and brand new, affordable homes prioritised for Waltham Forest residents.

decision_conditions: The materials to be used for the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted shall match those specified in the design and access statement received 2nd August 2024.

<p>The site management of the development hereby approved, including security enforcement, shall be maintained in accordance with the document titled Crime and Threat Mitigation Measures received 12th September 2024 and shall thereafter be retained as such for the lifetime of the development.</p>
<p>No goods delivered or collected by vehicles arriving at or departing from the site shall be unloaded or loaded on the public highway.<br></p>
<p>No music or amplified sound shall be audible outside the boundary of the Waltham Forest Town Hall and Fellowship Square complex.<br></p>
<p>The temporary use hereby approved shall only operate between the hours of 09:00-23:00 Monday to Saturday and 09:00-22:00 on Sundays and Public/Bank Holidays.<br></p>

<p>The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and thereafter maintained as such for the lifetime of the development:</p><ul><li>0040-SG-DR-A-10002 Rev P03&nbsp; Block Plan</li><li>0040-SG-DR-A-140001 Rev P03&nbsp; Proposed site plan</li><li>0040-SG-DR-A-140002 Rev P02&nbsp; Proposed roof plan</li><li>0040-SG-DR-A-140201 Rev P03&nbsp; Proposed site elevation front</li><li>0040-SG-DR-A-140202 Rev P02&nbsp; Proposed site elevation rear</li><li>0040-SG-DR-A-140203 Rev P02&nbsp; Proposed left elevation</li><li>0040-SG-DR-A-140204 Rev P02&nbsp; Proposed right elevation</li><li>0040-SG-DR-A-140301 Rev P03&nbsp; Proposed site section A</li></ul><p>dated 30th September 2024.<br></p>

<p>The temporary structures hereby permitted shall be erected for the period 25th November 2024 to 6th January 2025, after which the development and all paraphernalia shall be taken down and removed from the site and the original condition of the land reinstated until any operating dates for the following November-January period have been approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.</p>

<p>At least 8 weeks prior to subsequent annual commencement of the development hereby approved, its proposed operating dates shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The temporary structures shall only be erected for the approved dates and the total duration shall not exceed more than 6 weeks in any November-January period, after which the development and all paraphernalia shall be taken down and removed from the site and the original condition of the land reinstated.</p>
